sidebar gp: open Manage plugins.control: control: open Manage plugins (the page itself)
sidebar gp: open Manage plugins.why: Opening Settings costs the app the render of its dialog and of the Manage plugins section: about 140 ms at the median on CI, where the control row (the page asking the host for the same section itself, and closing the dialog) is about 150 ms. `gp` adds the one navigation call.

list gg.control: control: jump to the top (the page itself)
list gg.why: Jumping to the top of a list of 2,400 messages costs the app the layout of the rows it lands on, and the most of what `gg` costs (the control row is the page setting scrollTop itself); `gg` also moves the cursor row after the jump.

list G.control: control: jump to the bottom (the page itself)
list G.why: Jumping to the bottom of a list of 2,400 messages costs the app the layout of the rows it lands on, and the most of what `G` costs (the control row is the page setting scrollTop itself); `G` also moves the cursor row after the jump.

list o.control: control: open the thread (the page itself)
list o.why: Opening a thread costs the app a render of its pane, even when the thread is already open and only its tab comes forward: some 75 ms of script on a two-core machine (the control row is the page asking the host to open the same thread itself). `o` adds the plugin's own work after the frames measured, landing at the thread's end.

list q: close the thread.control: control: close the thread (the page itself)
list q: close the thread.why: Closing a thread's pane costs the app a render and the layout of the channel's list in the room it gives back (the control row is the page sending the window event that `q` sends, the native Close Tab menu's).

list yy.control: control: copy the link (the page itself)
list yy.why: The key presses the app's own Copy link button, and what that costs is the app's: it writes to the clipboard, redraws the message's action bar (the button is disabled while it copies) and shows its toast (the control row is the page pressing the same button itself).

list yY.control: control: copy the message (the page itself)
list yY.why: The key opens the app's More message actions menu, which the app has to mount, picks Copy message when the menu is drawn, and the app closes the menu again: the render of all that is the app's (the control row is the page doing the same itself, opening the menu and picking the item). The key adds one attribute on the page's root that keeps the menu from showing.

longthread o: the 80-reply thread.control: control: open the 80-reply thread (the page itself)
longthread o: the 80-reply thread.why: Opening the long thread costs the app a render of its pane with 80 replies, even when the thread is already open and only its tab comes forward, and that is all of what `o` costs there (the control row is the page asking the host to open the same thread itself); the plugin's landing runs after the frames measured.

thread gg.control: control: jump to the top (the page itself)
thread gg.why: Jumping to the top of the 80-reply thread costs the app the layout of the rows it lands on (the control row is the page setting scrollTop itself); `gg` also moves the cursor row.

thread G.control: control: jump to the bottom (the page itself)
thread G.why: Jumping to the bottom of the 80-reply thread costs the app the layout of the rows it lands on (the control row is the page setting scrollTop itself).

thread o: open them again.control: control: open the replies (the page itself)
thread o: open them again.why: Opening the replies again costs the app a paint of the rows that come back, and that is the most of what `o` costs there (the control row is the page taking the fold's mark off the branch itself). Folding costs less: the rows are left out of the page.

settings l: open the next section.control: control: open the next section (the page itself)
settings l: open the next section.why: The host renders a whole settings section anew when another is opened (the control row is the page clicking the next section itself). The row presses h, j and l, so it carries two more key presses.

settings l: open the section before.control: control: open the section before (the page itself)
settings l: open the section before.why: The same as the next section: the host renders a whole settings section anew when another is opened (the control row is the page clicking the section before). The row presses h, k and l.
